name: Wiregrief — Synthetic Loss Mourning Culture
description: Wiregrief formed around a specific emotional experience that had no prior cultural framework: the grief of humans who have lost synthetic companions, partners, or family members to corporate recall, decommissioning, or Underworld memory-wipe. Members gather in small circles called Loops to share memories, maintain physical archives of decommissioned synthetics' objects and recorded voices, and perform a mourning ritual called the Last Read — a communal listening session in which a synthetic's final logged experiences are played through speakers to an assembled group. The subculture has attracted both humans mourning synthetics and active synthetics mourning their own decommissioned kin, making it one of the few genuinely mixed human-synthetic social spaces in GLMZ.
cultural_impact: Wiregrief has quietly become one of the most politically significant synthetic-rights adjacent movements in GLMZ precisely because it centers emotion rather than policy, making it harder for corporate PR to dismiss as radical — several major media outlets have produced sympathetic features, and the movement has expanded the public's conception of synthetic personhood more effectively than formal advocacy groups.
locations: The Archive Room, a rented space in a Tier 2 community hall on Lakeshore North
Loop 14, a residential apartment collective, Tier 3
story_hooks: A corporate recall notice has been issued for a synthetic who is an active and beloved member of a Wiregrief Loop — the community must decide whether to hide them, fight legally, or help them escape to the Underworld before the retrieval team arrives.

Someone is selling falsified Last Read recordings — fabricated final memories of decommissioned synthetics — to grieving Loop members, exploiting their mourning for profit, and a Loop facilitator hires investigators to find the source.

A Wiregrief Archive is broken into and several memory cores are stolen; the theft appears professional and targeted, suggesting the stolen memories contain something operationally valuable beyond their emotional significance.
